svg.title: Tract 78: five records, one missing proof
svg.desc: Original Final Vestige Studios evidence-flow diagram for the Eusan family's Bohemia Spillway Tract 78. A 2012 Louisiana appellate opinion recounts the 1925 acquisition, DNR certification and August 2005 return, and affirms 996,596 dollars and 40 cents in revenues and 366,957 dollars and 12 cents in statutory interest while reversing a separate civil-fruits-interest award. The appellate opinion says the principal and statutory interest were accepted through joint trial stipulations, not a court inspection of underlying royalty ledgers, and does not establish cleared payments to the heirs. Each judicially attested step is distinguished from the unverified final payment.
svg.metadata: Creator: Final Vestige Studios; Date: 2026-11-16; Rights: © 2026 Final Vestige Studios. Original first-party explanatory vector, no external image assets. Source: Louisiana Fourth Circuit, Succession of Ursin (Eusan) v. Board of Levee Commissioners, 2012, https://law.justia.com/cases/louisiana/fourth-circuit-court-of-appeal/2012/2011-ca-1105.html . Diagram is a reconstruction of the documentary proof chain, NOT a historical photograph, direct inspection of the underlying deed, or evidence of payment. Caption: Tract 78's return and the resulting award are established in appellate reporting; the sums came through trial stipulations; neither an underlying itemized royalty ledger nor a cleared claimant disbursement has been independently inspected. Alt: Five vertically stacked checkpoints show 1925 acquisition, DNR heir certification, 2005 land return, 2012 court award, and missing verified payment record.
svg.text: A deed is not a receipt
